title: Leonardo CEO Mariani Sees Ukraine Unit as Acquisition Outpost
summary: Leonardo SpA, the Italian state-controlled defense company, is aiming to deepen ties with Ukraine’s fast-growing military-technology sector through its new Kyiv unit, seeking partnership, investment or acquisition opportunities, Chief Executive Officer Lorenzo Mariani said.

title: Philippines’ VP Duterte Posts Bail, Says She Fears for Her Life
summary: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail for a criminal case accusing her of threatening to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. She said she fears for her own life.

title: Europe’s Wealth Managers Are Turning Their Backs on Stock Rally
summary: More European wealth managers have turned pessimistic on the region’s stocks, taking the view that this year’s rally is likely to falter while markets in the US and developing countries power ahead.

title: Malaysia’s PAS Party Wants Nationwide Gambling License Review
summary: Parti Islam Se-Malaysia, which leads the country’s main opposition bloc, said the government should review existing gambling licenses and stop giving new ones, its latest effort to curb social ills.

title: HK’s Lee Says City to Expand Offshore Yuan Usage in 5-Year Plan
summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee said the city’s first five-year plan will focus on areas including expanding offshore yuan usage and cross-border investment with the mainland.

title: Bloom Energy, Illumina, Everpure to Join S&P 500 This Month
summary: Bloom Energy Corp., Illumina Inc. and Everpure Inc. will join the S&P 500 in the latest quarterly rebalance, S&P Dow Jones Indices said Friday.

title: Emerging Currencies Cap Longest Winning Streak Since 2007
summary: An index for emerging-market currencies rose for a 10th successive week, its longest winning streak since 2007, even as a blowout US jobs report briefly jolted global markets on Friday.

title: Wall Street Risk Complex Defies Rate Threat After Jobs Data
summary: The global bond selloff is proving no wrecking ball for Wall Street, repricing the cost of money without setting off the usual scramble out of risk assets.

title: Acuerdo de Trump con Venezuela inquieta a petroleras de EE.UU.
summary: El presidente Donald Trump se ha jactado de que su amplio acuerdo petrolero con Venezuela, que en la práctica da a Estados Unidos control sobre gran parte de la riqueza petrolera del país, es posiblemente “el mejor acuerdo jamás firmado”.

title: S&P Downgrades Senegal After Government Unveils Debt Rework
summary: S&P Global Ratings cut Senegal’s credit score further into junk territory, saying a distressed debt exchange or default on the country’s foreign-currency commercial debt is “extremely likely” after the government launched a plan to restructure its obligations.

title: S&P 500 Ends Week Flat as Strong Jobs Growth Fuels Fed-Hike Bets
summary: US stocks finished lower on Friday as the American economy ​added more jobs than expected in August, raising expectations that the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates soon.

title: Hedge Funds Hike Bullish Oil Bets to May High as Iran War Flares
summary: Hedge funds turned the most bullish on Brent crude since May as a fresh spate of fighting between the US and Iran heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Lutnick to Review Pentagon Deals Involving Cerberus Companies
summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been chosen by the Department of Defense to review any transactions between the Pentagon and companies associated with Cerberus Capital Management, according to a US official.

title: Dollar Posts Weekly Loss as Yen Jumps Amid Shifting Rate Bets
summary: The dollar slid to start September as mixed signals on the Federal Reserve’s next move kept traders on edge ahead of a pivotal inflation report, while a surging yen reverberated across global currency markets.

title: Algorithm Research CEO on Interest Rates Expectations
summary: Ketaki Sharma, founder and CEO of Algorithm Research, says the inflation is the main factor to watch in assessing the the bond market and the Federal Reserve’s next move. She speaks on "Horizons: Middle East and Africa." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Honey Deuces, Tickets, Merch: US Open Spending
summary: Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how people are spending their money at the US Open. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Fall as Jobs Fuel Bets Fed Will Raise Rates: Markets Wrap
summary: A stronger-than-anticipated increase in US jobs drove stocks and short-dated notes lower, with traders boosting their bets the Federal Reserve will raise rates this month.

title: Parents Push Teens to Start Investing Earlier Than They Did
summary: Bloomberg's Josyana Joshua joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Many parents are opening accounts that let teens learn the basics of investing with their supervision, in hopes of teaching them about investing early. As a result, financial firms have noticed and are rolling out products designed to appeal to parents and teens, such as joint brokerage accounts and parental-managed accounts that invest in exchange-traded funds. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Heinekin Highlights Nonalcoholic Beer, Serena Williams in US Open Partnership
summary: Maggie Timoney, CEO of Heinekin USA, said Heinekin's 0.0 nonalcoholic beer has seen success because consumers are looking to moderate their alcohol consumption, even if they're not looking to cut it out entirely. Timoney said that the beverage company wanted to honor the history of the US Open and the six championships won by Serena Williams in their partnership with the tennis star.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pulte’s Rewewed Attack on Credit Bureaus Sends FICO Plunging
summary: Shares of Fair Isaac Corp., Equifax Inc. and TransUnion tumbled on Friday after Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte renewed his long-standing criticism of the costs of consumer credit scores.
